title: B4 PUBLISH (the epic's point): the tier-1 records for the addendum's DIRECTIVEs and the recorded partial overruling of the T-344 reiteration framing, through the real CLI
description: This is the task the epic exists to make possible: the precedent layer amends itself through its own protocol. Publish, by running the real .harness/bin/precedent.py, the tier-1 records for the addendum's DIRECTIVE sections (its directives carry tier-1 operator authority under PRECEDENT.md's own ladder) AND the recorded PARTIAL OVERRULING of the T-344 reiteration-demotion framing per coordinator decision A2 - citing the DOI plus section, with reasoning included. The record ledger, the subject slugs, the tier evidence anchors, the operation types and the sources tokens are all fixed by docs/precedent-research/synthesis-v1-requirements.md; your job is to execute it faithfully and report exactly what the CLI did. Depends on T-353 (the v2 schema, the DOI token grammar and the overruling anchor mechanism must exist before a v2 record can be minted) and on T-356 (every record cites an interpretive code version, and you cannot cite a version of a document that does not exist). Runs concurrently with T-355: disjoint record ids, guarded allocation.
acceptance_criteria: OWNS EXACTLY: the NEW records it mints under .harness/precedents/ (PR-005 and higher). Do NOT edit PR-001..PR-004 (T-355 owns the migration and may be running concurrently), do NOT edit .harness/bin/precedent.py, PRECEDENT.md, INTERPRETIVE-CODE.md, .harness/precedents/README.md or any test file.

NEVER HAND-WRITE A RECORD. Every record is minted by running the real CLI. A hand-edited or hand-created JSON file under .harness/precedents/ is an automatic REJECT: the entire point of this task is that the layer amends itself through its own protocol, and a hand-written record is the silent divergence the layer exists to forbid.

PUBLISH THE LEDGER THE SYNTHESIS FIXED: one tier-1 record per addendum DIRECTIVE section per the record ledger in docs/precedent-research/synthesis-v1-requirements.md, plus the A2 partial-overruling record. For every addendum section 2 through 7 that does NOT receive its own record, state in the handoff which record subsumes it or why none is needed. A section silently skipped is a defect.

EVERY RECORD CARRIES, without exception: `sources` including the DOI token for the addendum (10.22201/iij.24487937e.2026.20.20316 plus the section, in the exact token form the synthesis fixed) - NEVER the local docs/ path, which is gitignored (.gitignore:33) and would dangle for every reader who clones the repo; the typed operation per A4; `interpretive_code_version` citing INTERPRETIVE-CODE.md v1; `validity_conditions` distinct from `scope_conditions`; authority_tier 1 with `tier_evidence` naming the operator-directive anchor the synthesis fixed.

THE A2 RECORD IS THE EPIC'S POINT AND MUST BE RECOGNIZABLY AN OVERRULING, NOT A RESTATEMENT. It partially overrules the T-344 framing recorded as R-2 in docs/precedent-research/synthesis-refinements.md ('Repeated confirmation becomes a separate, non-binding reiterated flag on tier-4 records'). It must carry the reasoning A2 states, including the preserved half: T-344's argument that any N>1 threshold is a de facto ban on binding is PRESERVED and untouched - reiteration is now a first-class force-raising mechanism, authority_tier remains issuance authority, a single verdicted decision still binds, and what changes is the CEILING, not the floor. It must use the anchor mechanism the synthesis fixed for targeting a decision that is not itself a PR record. If that anchor mechanism does not work when you run it, that is a REJECT-level finding against T-353 to be reported in a blocked handoff - never worked around by hand-editing a file.

ACCEPTANCE COMMANDS, exactly, ALL quoted verbatim in the handoff with their full stdout and exit codes (P-025): for each record, the COMPLETE `python3 .harness/bin/precedent.py publish --agent <you> --task T-358 ...` line exactly as run, with no elision and no ellipsis - a verifier must be able to paste it and re-run it in a temp root. Then `python3 .harness/bin/precedent.py show PR-NNN` (exit 0) for every minted id. Then `python3 .harness/bin/precedent.py cite PR-NNN` (exit 0) for every minted id. Then `python3 .harness/bin/precedent.py cite --all` and `python3 .harness/bin/precedent.py conflicts` against the live registry with exit codes and complete findings.

EXPLAIN EVERY NEW FINDING: the live-registry baseline before your work is exactly one conflicts finding - PR-001's dangling P-023 token, which is the layer correctly reporting a real constitutional gap. Any ADDITIONAL finding your records introduce must be explained in the handoff, not absorbed. A dangling DOI token means your source token form does not match what T-353 implemented.

`python3 -m unittest discover -s .harness/tests -p "test_precedent*.py" -v` must still be green after all your publishes, with the 'Ran N tests' line quoted - publishing into the live registry must not break the seed or migration tests.

MUST NOT SELF-CONFIRM: every record publishes with confirmation_status unconfirmed and confirmed_by null. Scope claims do not bind until a DISTINCT identity confirms them (SDR-02), and you are the producer. A producer-confirmed record is an automatic REJECT.

MUST NOT write .harness/state.json - in particular no P-023 evolution.accepted_mutations backfill, which is a tier-2 constitutional act requiring the section 5A loop plus the human gate (ORCHESTRATION.md:225-229) and is escalated at the epic join, never performed here - and MUST NOT write .harness/blackboard.json outside blackboard.py.

Hand off with `python3 .harness/bin/blackboard.py handoff --to-role verifier --agent <you>` (never self-mark done). The note carries: the complete command transcript, the record ledger as a table (record id -> addendum section or coordinator decision -> operation type -> sources tokens), and every OPEN-QUESTION the act of publishing exposed - especially anything the synthesis left underdetermined that you had to resolve at the keyboard.
